title: Git LFS
description: Store large files outside the history – for this repository.

progress.label: Progress of fetching the LFS files

patterns.label: Patterns stored via LFS
patterns.heading: Patterns
patterns.empty: No pattern goes through LFS yet. Enter an extension or a folder below.

readFailed: The state of Git LFS couldn't be read

missing.title: Git LFS isn't installed on this computer
missing.body: Git LFS stores large files (images, videos, archives) outside the history; the repository then only contains a small pointer. Install it from git-lfs.com or through your package manager, then check again – no restart needed.
missing.used_one: This repository uses LFS for {{count}} pattern. Without Git LFS you only see the pointers instead of these files, and new files end up in the normal history by accident.
missing.used_other: This repository uses LFS for {{count}} patterns. Without Git LFS you only see the pointers instead of these files, and new files end up in the normal history by accident.
missing.unused: This repository doesn't use LFS so far, so you're not missing anything here.

rejected: Git LFS doesn't accept this pattern.
intro: From the next commit on, Git stores files matching a pattern in LFS storage; the history only contains a pointer. The patterns are kept in .gitattributes and apply to everyone who clones the repository.

newPattern.label: New pattern
newPattern.hint: An extension (*.psd) or a folder (images/**), written as in .gitignore.

footer: “Fetch” replaces pointers in the working directory with the real files from the remote. “Clean up” deletes old LFS files from local storage that the current state doesn't need.

locks.heading: Locks
locks.intro: A lock tells everyone working on this repository that you’re editing a file. The LFS server keeps the locks; they’re read again after every fetch.
locks.refreshLabel: Read the locks from the server again
locks.unsupported: The LFS server of this repository doesn’t offer file locking.
